title: Confirmed: no UI path to raise a tier quota on an ON_SALE event (regression vs develop)
evidence: The edit page returns 'Không thể chỉnh sửa sự kiện' whenever !canEditEvent(state) (edit-event-client.tsx:22), and EDITABLE_STATES is DRAFT/SCHEDULED/REJECTED (organizer-service.ts). event-list.tsx and moderation-status-card.tsx hide the Edit link for ON_SALE. No other component calls updateTierQuota (grep: only edit-event-client.tsx:45). On develop (2970b7f) the edit page rendered the wizard for ON_SALE events, and event-wizard.tsx (isCurrentOnSale, line 203) blocked decreases and allowed increases. That branch is now dead code. AC-22 says 'on ON_SALE a quota decrease is blocked client-side', which only makes sense if an ON_SALE quota change is reachable, and the backend allows ON_SALE increases (contracts §2 PUT .../tiers/{tierId}). The new edit page test (page.test.tsx:96) asserts ON_SALE is refused, which locks in the regression.
repro: Open /organizer/events/{id}/edit for an ON_SALE event: you get the 'cannot edit' card and no quota field. On develop the wizard opened with quota-only edits.
fix: Add a quota-only mode for ON_SALE (and SOLD_OUT if the backend allows it). Either render the wizard tier step with the event fields read-only, skip updateOrganizerEvent (PUT /events is not allowed on ON_SALE), and call only updateTierQuota; or add a small 'Tăng số lượng vé' form on review-status. Show the edit link for ON_SALE events, and update the it.each test so ON_SALE expects the quota-only form.

title: After a partial create failure, clicking submit again creates a second draft event
evidence: When createOrganizerEvent returns failedStep, the page returns {error, failedStep, draftHref} and the wizard only shows the partial alert (event-wizard.tsx:273). The 'Lưu nháp' and 'Gửi kiểm duyệt' buttons stay enabled (event-wizard.tsx:596-606, disabled only while isSubmitting), and the wizard has no record that the event already exists. Clicking either button calls createOrganizerEvent(data) again, which does POST /api/v1/events again: a duplicate draft (or a 409/422 slug conflict if the user typed a slug).
repro: Mock POST /api/v1/events -> 201 {id:E1}, POST /tiers -> 422, then click 'Gửi kiểm duyệt' twice. The second click makes a second POST /api/v1/events. A test asserting exactly one POST /api/v1/events after two clicks fails today.
fix: When the result has a draftHref (or failedStep), disable the submit buttons and leave only the 'Mở bản nháp' link, or redirect to the edit page automatically. Alternatively, keep the created event id in page state and resume (tiers/submit) against it instead of creating again.

title: Edit retry after a partial tier failure re-POSTs tiers that were already created
evidence: existingTiers = new Map(event.tiers...) comes from the initial load and is never refreshed. Take two new tiers A and B: A is POSTed, B fails, and the error is returned. The wizard keeps both tiers with their local ids, so on resubmit A is still missing from the map and addTier(A) runs again -> 422 duplicate name. The recovery link draftHref is the same URL (/organizer/events/{id}/edit). A next/link to the current route does not remount OrganizerEventView, so its useEffect does not reload the event. The user is stuck until a hard reload.
repro: Edit a DRAFT event and add new tiers A and B. Mock POST tiers: A -> 201, B -> 422. Fix B, then click 'Lưu nháp' again: POST tiers A is sent a second time and gets 422.
fix: After a partial failure, reload the event (call OrganizerEventView's load/setEvent with fresh data, or router.refresh plus a key change) and map created tiers back to their server ids. At minimum, record the tiers created in this session and skip them on retry. Point draftHref somewhere that forces a reload, or drop it on the edit page.

title: Edit wizard offers 'Gửi kiểm duyệt' for SCHEDULED events, which always fails with 422
evidence: The step-4 footer always renders the submit-for-review button. edit-event-client.tsx:56 then calls submitOrganizerEvent, but SUBMITTABLE_STATES is DRAFT/REJECTED only. For a SCHEDULED event the PUT succeeds and the user sees 'Đã lưu ... nhưng bước gửi kiểm duyệt thất bại'.
repro: Edit a SCHEDULED event and click 'Gửi kiểm duyệt': the backend returns 422 and the partial-failure alert appears.
fix: Pass a canSubmit prop (canSubmitEvent(initialEvent.state)) to the wizard and hide or disable the submit-for-review button when it is false.

title: An expired session (refresh failed) during join or poll is shown as a network error, not 'sign in again'
evidence: joinQueue/fetchQueueStatus go through apiFetch. When the refresh fails, apiFetch throws ApiError('AUTH_REQUIRED'), which is not a QueueError. waiting-room.tsx then falls into the else branch: 'Đã xảy ra lỗi mạng khi tham gia phòng chờ'. use-queue-status.ts:243 counts it as a network failure, sets connection 'reconnecting'/'offline' and retries with backoff. The checkout view has a dedicated AUTH_REQUIRED alert, but the waiting room does not. The i18n key waiting.signInRequired was added but is never used.
repro: Store a session whose access token is expired, make POST /auth/refresh return 401, and open /waiting/{id}: the network-error text appears instead of a sign-in prompt.
fix: In waiting-room, handle err instanceof ApiError && err.code === 'AUTH_REQUIRED' (show t('waiting.signInRequired') with a sign-in link). In use-queue-status, treat AUTH_REQUIRED as terminal (update error, transport idle).

title: cancelHold exists but nothing in the UI calls it
evidence: grep for cancelHold in non-test sources finds only its definition. Checkout and payment have no 'release seats' action, so a buyer who leaves keeps the hold until the TTL ends. AC-11 only requires the function, so this is a gap rather than a violation.
fix: Optional: add a 'Huỷ giữ vé' action in OrderSummary or the payment page that calls cancelHold(hold.holdId) and then resetHold(). Otherwise record it as follow-up.

title: Any 409 from POST /payments is mapped to HOLD_EXPIRED, including idempotency-in-progress
evidence: initiatePayment maps every 409 to HOLD_EXPIRED without reading the problem type. usePaymentSession then sets holdExpired=true and clearActiveHold(eventId). The idempotency middleware also returns 409 urn:eventflow:problem:idempotency-in-progress (contracts §0). hold-client already tells the two apart (hold-client.ts:185), but payment-client does not. The spec §5 edge case ('idempotent retry after 409 in-flight (Retry-After)') is not handled for holds or payments: the UI shows a message but never retries.
repro: Mock POST /v1/events/{id}/payments -> 409 {type:'urn:eventflow:problem:idempotency-in-progress'} with Retry-After: 1. The UI declares the hold expired and wipes the local hold.
fix: Read the problem type. For idempotency-in-progress, throw AMBIGUOUS, or wait Retry-After and retry once with the same key. Keep HOLD_EXPIRED for the other 409s.

title: Logout while a refresh is in flight brings the session back
evidence: doRefresh calls setSession(next) after the refresh response arrives, without checking that the session still exists. If logout() runs clearSession() while a refresh is pending (for example a background poll triggered the proactive refresh), the refresh response then writes a new token pair back into storage. useAuth sees ef:session, and the user appears logged in again with a valid refresh token.
repro: Start a request with an access token within 30 s of expiry so the refresh is pending, call logout() before the refresh resolves, then let it resolve: getSession() is non-null.
fix: Before setSession in doRefresh, re-read storage. If there is no session, or its refresh token is no longer cur.refreshToken, discard the result and throw AUTH_REQUIRED. Alternatively, keep a logout epoch counter and compare it.

title: A failed proactive refresh (network/5xx) blocks a request whose token is still valid
evidence: apiFetch awaits refreshAccessToken when exp <= 30 s. If that refresh throws NETWORK_ERROR or HTTP_5xx, the error propagates and the original request is never sent, even though the access token may still be valid for up to 30 s. The spec says expiry is only a hint (§5 clock skew). Hold and payment callers turn this into AMBIGUOUS/NETWORK_ERROR.
repro: Set an access token with exp = now + 20 s, make POST /auth/refresh reject with a network error, and call apiFetch('/v1/orders/x'): it rejects without fetching /v1/orders/x.
fix: Wrap the proactive refresh in try/catch. On a non-AUTH_REQUIRED error, continue with the current token and let the 401 token-expired path handle real expiry.

title: Issue-ticket idempotency key is kept after a 2xx with no QR tickets, so retries replay the same empty response
evidence: forgetIssueKey runs only on non-2xx responses. If issue-tickets returns 200 with tickets lacking qr_payload (filtered out at line 401) or with an empty list, useIssuedTickets retries with the same stored key. The idempotency middleware replays the cached 2xx body, so every retry gets the same empty result until the attempts run out. retry() does not reset the key either.
repro: Mock the first POST issue-tickets -> 200 {tickets:[]} and later calls -> 200 with tickets, then simulate a middleware replay by keying the response on Idempotency-Key: the tickets never show.
fix: Call forgetIssueKey(orderId) when the filtered list is empty, and also in useIssuedTickets.retry().

title: PAID header says 'Vé điện tử của bạn đã sẵn sàng!' while the tickets are still pending or failed
evidence: The success card is shown for every PAID order, alongside the 'Đang phát hành vé' spinner or the 'Chưa lấy được vé điện tử' warning. The 'Vé điện tử của bạn ({quantity} vé)' header also renders before any ticket exists.
repro: Render a PAID order with issueTickets pending: both 'đã sẵn sàng' and 'Đang phát hành vé' are visible.
fix: Show 'đã sẵn sàng' only when issued.tickets.length > 0. Otherwise show 'Thanh toán thành công — đang phát hành vé'.
